summary.headline: BASF India FY26 PBT before exceptionals rose to Rs 564 crore from Rs 600 crore equivalent comparison; Q4 PBT Rs 90 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.
summary.overview: Management presented FY26 (year to 31 March 2026) consolidated results, including the coatings business and discontinued operations, with sales around Rs 3,900-4,000 crore per quarter and volumes up 6-7% for the year but prices down 5-6%. Q4 showed volume-led growth (about 12-15% volume growth YoY, sales up about 10%) and PBT before exceptionals of Rs 90 crore against Rs 25 crore in March 2025. Working capital rose about Rs 600-800 crore, pushing FY26 operating cash flow to about minus Rs 110 crore versus Rs 370 crore last year. Management flagged the West Asia conflict, feedstock inflation, rupee depreciation and a possible demand softening in the coming months, and said no plants were shut down.

segments.name: Materials
segments.commentary: Largest segment (almost one-third of sales); sales down on volume and price, but PBT improved by Rs 27 crore. Celesto (PU bumpers) is about 10% of the performance materials division.

segments.name: Nutrition and Care
segments.commentary: Only segment with both volume and price growth; PBT before exceptionals fell from Rs 65 crore to Rs 31 crore due to market competition.

segments.name: Industry Solutions (dispersions, performance chemicals, process catalysts)
segments.commentary: Volumes up with significant price pressure; dispersions drove the largest PBT improvement in the segment group.

segments.name: Agriculture Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue down about Rs 120 crore to near Rs 2,000 crore (about 12% of total); volumes down slightly, prices up; market share held at about 7%.

segments.name: Surface Technologies (coatings)
segments.commentary: Sales about Rs 595 crore (about 4% of consolidated); PBT about Rs 3 crore vs minus Rs 7 crore; being sold to Carlyle.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Pure merchandise business; volume up, PBT slightly lower.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal forecasts or guidance; said demand is likely to soften slightly and a wait-and-see mode is emerging in some sectors.
Priority is passing higher input costs into prices, starting upstream; pass-through is uneven by segment and takes time to reach downstream.
Agro: no forward view on FY27 volumes or price hikes; team said to be prepared for the Kharif season, with monsoon and West Asia conflict as key uncertainties.
Celesto expansion: building complete; line to go live by end of CY2026. Dispersion Line 3 (Mangalore, 15% dispersion capacity increase) targeted for commissioning by end of next year.
Agro demerger: SEBI/exchange clearance on 2 February 2026; shareholder meeting 24 June 2026; share entitlement ratio 1:1.
Coatings sale to Carlyle (valuation Rs 230.16 crore) expected to close by Q2 CY2026; BASF to retain 40% stake post-closing.
capex_capacity: Celesto expansion (Materials, Dahej): about Rs 150 crore spent in FY26, roughly Rs 150-170 crore more to be spent; go-live targeted by end of CY2026.
Dispersion Line 3 in Mangalore: groundbreaking February 2026; adds about 15% dispersion capacity; commissioning targeted by end of next year. This would be the 5th dispersion line in India.
FY27 total capex expected to be more than Rs 200 crore including Celesto, dispersion line 3 and maintenance capex.
Maintenance capex typically about Rs 80-100 crore per year.
No large new capex beyond these projects announced; management said it is looking at India expansion opportunities but too early to comment.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in FY26 was about 6-7% while prices fell about 5-6%; margin compression came from input costs and product mix.
Upstream input costs (oil, gas, feedstock) rose after the West Asia conflict began end-February 2026; pass-through to customers is partial and segment-dependent.
Management expects a slight softening of demand; some pre-buying during the crisis is reversing.
Agro: Chinese oversupply, erratic monsoon and lower chilli acreage hit volumes; high channel inventory; 12 launches in last four years now about 25% of agro sales.
Competition from Chinese oversupply in upstream chemicals and generic competition in corn herbicides was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why have agro margins compressed over FY25-FY26 despite new launches, and are these the normalised margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited erratic monsoons, soft commodity prices (chilli acreage and intensity down), and high channel inventories. It said the 12 launches in four years are about 25% of ag sales and carry higher margins, and that channel inventory is healthy. It gave no view on normalised margins.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material cost increases being passed on, and is demand responding?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through starts upstream and is uneven by segment; management has been successful in some cases. It expects a slight softening of demand as customers wait and see and pre-buying fades.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new CAPEX planned, and how much will be spent in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No large capex beyond Celesto and Dispersion Line 3 (plus maintenance); management said FY26 capex was about Rs 200 crore, and FY27 capex would be more than Rs 200 crore. Land/new site investment was described as too early to discuss.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the coatings business valued at about 0.25x sales versus 2x globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is not comparable to the German one. The independent valuation used DCF, giving Rs 230.16 crore, because on an EBITDA basis the business is roughly break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Why have royalty and service payments to the parent risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Royalty rates range from 1.5% to 13% by product maturity. Royalty was about Rs 130 crore last year and about Rs 156-160 crore this year. Service charges rose with the Kuala Lumpur shared service centre, and IT charges are about Rs 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 EBITDA of Rs 656 crore comparable with FY21 at Rs 633 crore, and should investors expect growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY21 is not comparable due to restructuring, including the sale of the construction chemicals business. It cited Chinese oversupply and weak consumer spending as headwinds, and said the focus is profitable growth and value unlocking via the agro demerger and coatings sale.

risks_watch: Feedstock and energy cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, plus rupee depreciation, versus the pace of price pass-through.
Working capital: receivables up and payables down (Rs 3,800 crore vs Rs 4,200 crore); FY26 operating cash flow about minus Rs 110 crore.
Agro Kharif season: monsoon, channel inventory and farm-gate demand; FY26 agro volumes down; demerger shareholder vote on 24 June 2026.
Coatings sale to Carlyle closing by Q2 CY2026 subject to approvals; agro demerger timeline.
Operating expense (fixed cost) growth flagged by management as a focus area; Nutrition and Care PBT down sharply.
Two lost-time injuries (Dahej, February and March 2026); no high-severity or process safety incidents.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and operational resilience (no shutdowns), but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined forward guidance and flagged demand softening, input cost pressure and difficulty in forecasting the monsoon and the conflict. Evasive on capex beyond the announced projects and on the agro FY27 outlook.
key_quotes: And you will see that the last quarter of the fiscal year was very, very robust.
So we have paid some of the dues in the last quarter, and that has reduced the accounts payable from 4,200 crores to 3,800 crores.
As of 31st of March, 2026, the said business generated sales of 595 crores, representing around 4% of the consolidated sales of BASF India Limited.
Fortunately, we did not have to shut down any operations.
